newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: BOTSWANA STOCKS WEEK- BANK STOCKS CONTINUE TO GAIN.
newsitem.headline: BOTSWANA STOCKS WEEK- BANK STOCKS CONTINUE TO GAIN.

text.p: The Botswana Stock Exchange
surged further last week on the back of the continuing rise in
bank stocks.
The market is now 90 percent higher in U.S. dollar terms
than on January 2.
Standard Chartered Bank of Botswana put on 350 thebe
to close at 1,350 thebe, while Barclays Bank of
Botswana added 70 thebe to 1,400 thebe.
The two bank stocks now amount for 40 per cent of the
bourse's market capitalisation and vice-chairman Andrew Ashton
said he believed the counters had yet to peak.
"There is a stong possibility of further advances," he said.
"We are seeing more liquidity as sellers take profits."
Standard Chartered traded 22,950 shares over the week and
Barclays 10,000.
In non-bank share trade 1.37 milliion shares in brewery
holding company Sechaba Trust traded as domestic
institutions decided to take profits from the share's strong run
this year. The counter put on 20 thebe to 480 thebe.
Milling company and food wholesaler Sefalana
Holdings dropped 10 thebe as it went ex-dividend with a
small trade of 1,300 shares and closed at 530 thebe, while
clothing chain Pep Holdings traded a 200 share parcel to
stay unchanged at 375 thebe.
Volume and value were down, with 1.4 million shares worth
6.99 million pula changing hands compared with the previous
week's 1.5 million shares worth 8.32 million pula.
The domestic index put on 58.9 points to close at 677.74
points.
On the foreign board De Beers saw a strong rise in
its bid price to 13,716 thebe and closed up 688 thebe at 13,923
thebe.
The all companies index added 19.91 points to 435.19 points.
